Name: SDV-Radiance
Author: PHUICMT
Description:
[center][size=5]SDV-Radiance[/size]
[b]A full lighting and post-processing suite for Stardew Valley, in one mod.[/b]

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/49397/49397-1786022210-456083196.png[/img][/center]
[color=#D4D4D8]
Shadows, water reflections, sun shafts, weather drawn as weather, particles, indoor light and colour grading, in one GPU layer that [b]reads the frame your game already drew[/b], so recolours, custom sprites and map mods just work. Every effect has its own switch and sliders, previewed live in the in-game tuner ([b]F6[/b]) and in GMCM.

Measured here across six scenes it costs 0.27 to 0.70 ms a frame, at worst 4% of a 60 fps frame, and [font=Courier New]radiance_report[/font] prints the same breakdown for your own machine. Three one-click quality presets and a ten-second benchmark are on the Performance tab.

[size=5]🆕 New in 1.6.2[/size][/color]
[list]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]A choice of water.[/b] The water page opens with one pick: [b]1.6.2 water or Classic[/b]. Classic is the water of every release so far, untouched. The new one moves the image with a spectrum of travelling ripples anchored at the waterline, fades toward the water's own colour with depth like a photograph of a lake, and shifts as you walk the way an image under the surface really does. Nine dials of its own.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Waterfalls churn.[/b] The pool under a fall reflects nothing at the foot and settles back over a few tiles, and a stream's reflection eases off before the lip.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Creatures draw their own reflections.[/b] Ducks, babies, animals in hats: the mirror asks them to draw it instead of guessing from their sheet. A duck's reflection sat 33 pixels below the duck; it touches now. A creature that lives below the surface gets no reflection at all.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]The Ginger Island boat is out of the water.[/b] The mod records what every map paints for itself and keeps the ripple off it, parrots included.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Windows come back on building repaints.[/b] Labels are filed per piece of art, not per sheet name, so a repaint gets its own answer about which panes are glass.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]A falling leaf is bent by the water's own wave[/b], everywhere, one dial from flat to exactly as much as the water.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Storm rain is thicker than plain rain[/b], the rain's slant is a dial, and the angle petals fall at is its own dial.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Colour banding on water is gone[/b], and the flicker on its band edges with it, for every look.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]How flat the ground lies[/b] under a shadow is a dial, with a separate one for people, and the tuner now highlights the chosen option in every row of choices.[/color][/*]
[/list][color=#D4D4D8]
[size=5]📸 See it[/size]
Every pair is the [b]same frame twice[/b], mod off on the left and on on the right. The world art is not vanilla; see the note at the bottom of this section.[/color]

[color=#D4D4D8][size=3][b]About these screenshots[/b][/size]
[i]The world art is not vanilla: DaisyNiko's Earthy Recolour and Tilesheets, Stardew Valley Expanded, Water Flow, the Forever Falls Farm map, and Fashion Sense outfits. They also use the author's own settings rather than the shipped defaults: colour grading is on with a warm look (ships off), and the water ripples harder than a fresh install. Both are switches in F6.[/i][/color][/center]
[/spoiler]
[color=#D4D4D8]
[size=5]✨ What it does[/size]

[b]Lighting and shadows[/b][/color]
[list]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Directional shadows[/b] from the real sprite silhouettes, leaning and stretching with the sun, [b]moonlight shadows[/b] at night by lunar phase, and [b]per-light indoor shadows[/b] from every lamp, torch and fireplace, up to 48 lights a scene.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Occlusion-aware GI[/b]: warm light pools around real sources and is blocked by walls, so flat interiors get depth.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Painted light sources[/b]: art marked as glowing (a lit sign, a forge) emits its own colour; labelled windows glow after dusk and lay [b]daylight patches[/b] across the floor by hour, season and weather. Rooms follow the clock from cool dawn to warm evening.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]The scene answers lightning[/b]: shadows kick away from the bolt, the darkening lifts with the flash, a warm afterglow follows.[/color][/*]
[/list][color=#D4D4D8]
[b]Water[/b][/color]
[list]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Two waters, your pick[/b]: the 1.6.2 water (ripple spectrum, depth fade, camera parallax, churning waterfalls) or Classic with its three looks, each showing only its own dials.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Pixel-accurate reflections[/b] along the real painted shoreline, not tile edges; your own reflection follows you into shallow water; crab pots, splashes and the bobber reflect too.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Caustics[/b] on the shallow bed, [b]rain rings[/b] on the surface, and ripple that adapts to pond or ocean, weather and season.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Accurate detection[/b] from what the game actually draws plus a hand-painted label set, so modded water lines up; ice, flowing water, waterfalls and lava each read differently.[/color][/*]
[/list][color=#D4D4D8]
[b]Weather and particles[/b][/color]
[list]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Rain, snow and windblown leaves at three depths[/b], splashes where drops land, storm density, rain slant and petal fall angle as dials, and [b]visible lightning bolts[/b] on any map.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Drops on the edge of the screen[/b] that merge, grow heavy and run, becoming frost in snow.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Particles drawn into the world[/b]: dust in a window beam, sparks off the fire, fireflies, blossom and leaves that bend with the water's own wave, sparks around a glow ring.[/color][/*]
[/list][color=#D4D4D8]
[b]Atmosphere and colour[/b][/color]
[list]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Sun shafts[/b] cut from what actually blocks the light, on by default; [b]lamp shafts[/b] on their own switch, shipped off (see Known issues).[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Cloud shadows[/b], [b]day fog and night mist[/b], [b]bloom[/b], [b]tilt-shift[/b], [b]vignette[/b], subtle [b]chromatic aberration[/b].[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Colour grading[/b] by time, weather and season with metered auto-exposure, seven ready-made looks and a slot for your own LUT. [b]Ships off[/b]: the colour of somebody's game is not a thing to change unasked. F6, first tab, one click. A [b]blue light filter[/b] rides on top.[/color][/*]
[/list][color=#D4D4D8]
[size=5]🎛️ Fully configurable[/size]
[b]F6[/b] opens the live tuner: sixteen tabs, drag any slider and watch the world update, save named looks, or pick Subtle / Cinematic / Vibrant. Everything is also in [b]Generic Mod Config Menu[/b], and every single effect can be switched off individually.[/color]

[center][img width=430]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/49397/49397-1786025856-1835987342.png[/img] [img width=430]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/49397/49397-1786025099-202740560.png[/img][/center]
[color=#D4D4D8]
[size=5]⚠️ Known issues[/size][/color]
[list]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Water and glass detection[/b] come from the game's own data plus a hand-painted label set. Since 1.6.2 labels are filed per piece of art, so repaints get their own answers; what is still missing (a boat deck, an unlabelled window in a map mod) gets filled in as reports come in, and nothing breaks in the meantime. [font=Courier New]radiance_report[/font] names the sheet.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Whether water carries under a given bridge[/b] depends on how that map built the bridge; a report with [font=Courier New]radiance_report[/font] from on top of it is the one thing a screenshot cannot tell me.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Lamp shafts ship off[/b]: they still treat bright surfaces as light sources, so a large pale sprite can blow out. The sun shafts are a different method and ship on.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]SpriteMaster / Clear Glasses: incompatible[/b], pick one. [b]Clear Monocle works[/b]; its author shipped explicit support in July.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]A modded creature can sit a few pixels above its reflection[/b] when its art paints splash or feet below the waterline; telling those from a tail would cut the legs off something else, so the few pixels stay.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]An invisible mossy tree in winter is a vanilla sheet fault[/b], not this mod's: the game asks for a sprite column past the sheet's edge. This mod steps the rectangle back so the tree draws without its moss instead of not at all.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Online co-op has had less testing than split screen[/b]; the code is shared, the two-machine session is not. [font=Courier New]radiance_report[/font] plus [font=Courier New]radiance_screenwatch[/font] collect what I need.[/color][/*]
[/list][color=#D4D4D8]
[size=5]🔭 In development[/size][/color]
[list]
[*][color=#D4D4D8]Puddles decided from the map, which is what keeps the wet ground out of the menus.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8]The god-ray rebuild carried over to the lamp shafts.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8]Per-light shadows extended to objects and map props.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8]Water carrying under every bridge and pier, not only the ones whose map data allows it today.[/color][/*]
[/list][color=#D4D4D8]
[size=5]📦 Installation[/size]
Install [url=https://smapi.io/]SMAPI[/url], unzip into [font=Courier New]Mods[/font], play. [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/5098]Generic Mod Config Menu[/url] is optional but recommended. Safe to add or remove mid-save.

[size=5]⚙️ Performance[/size]
One capture, one shader chain, cached between frames; it runs on the rendered image, so your other mods barely affect it. Measured on this machine (Core Ultra 7, RTX 5080, 720p uncapped): [b]0.27 ms a frame indoors, 0.70 ms at the worst[/b], a beach in the rain with everything on, which is 4% of a 60 fps frame. Treat those as a floor, not a promise, and measure your own: [font=Courier New]radiance_report[/font] prints the cost line by line with nothing to switch on first. The Performance tab has three presets, an effect resolution slider, a ten-second benchmark, and the shadows-per-character setting, which is the most direct lever on the heaviest part. [b]Switching an effect off gives its cost straight back[/b]; that is measured, not assumed.

[size=5]🧩 Compatibility[/size][/color]
[list]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Appearance mods just work[/b]: everything is generated from what is actually rendered. Tested alongside SVE and 80+ mod setups.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Weather mods[/b]: if another mod claimed the game's weather drawing, this one stands down there.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Global God Rays[/b]: works together; the two cover similar ground, so run both and turn one down, or run either.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Multiplayer and split screen[/b]: client-side, only you need it; other players cast shadows and reflect, and each screen keeps its own data.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]SpriteMaster / Clear Glasses: incompatible[/b] (orange or black world on load, dead patches of mirror). [b]Clear Monocle works.[/b] Other post-processing mods (Dynamic Shader, ReShade) overlap; run one at a time for a predictable look. [b]Android: not tested.[/b][/color][/*]
[/list][color=#D4D4D8]
[size=5]❓ FAQ[/size][/color]
[list]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Safe to uninstall?[/b] Yes, it touches no save data. No network calls, no telemetry.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]I updated and nothing changed.[/b] Your [font=Courier New]config.json[/font] is kept on purpose. Delete it for the new defaults, or press F6 and pick a preset.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Something looks off with mod X?[/b] Post a [url=https://smapi.io/log]SMAPI log[/url], a screenshot, and the file [font=Courier New]radiance_report[/font] writes while you stand in the spot, on the Bugs tab. The command output beats both.[/color][/*]
[/list][color=#D4D4D8]
[size=5]🙏 Credits[/size]
Built on SMAPI, MonoGame and Generic Mod Config Menu; effects reimplemented from scratch, see CREDITS in the download. Thanks to the Stardew modding community.

[size=5]☕ Support[/size]
Free and always will be. If it brightened your farm: [/color][url=https://ko-fi.com/phuicmt]ko-fi.com/phuicmt[/url]
[color=#D4D4D8]
[size=5]🌏 Languages[/size]
Bundled: English, Thai, Simplified Chinese (complete, by [url=https://forums.nexusmods.com/profile/194031764-rime961/]rime961[/url]). Also on the Nexus: Korean by [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/49448]jjongleee[/url] and a [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/49647]Chinese translation[/url] by Rubbish404. Text keys still change between updates; every changelog lists them under "For translators". Huge thanks to everyone translating this mod. ♥[/color]
